chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Hanan ibn Sadir who said:
I, my father, Abu Hamza al-Thumali, Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir, and Ziyad al-Ahlam entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).
He saw Ziyad whose body had shed its hair (from shaving the head for Ihram), so he said to him, "From where did you enter Ihram?" He said, "From Kufa."
He said, "And why did you enter Ihram from Kufa?" He said, "It reached me from one of you that he said: 'That which is far from the Ihram is greater in reward.'"
He said, "Only a liar has conveyed this to you."
Then he said to Abu Hamza, "From where did you enter Ihram?" He said, "From al-Rabadhah."
He said to him, "And why?" He said, "Because you heard that the grave of Abu Dharr is there, so you loved to pass by it."
Then he said to my father and Abd al-Rahim, "From where did you both enter Ihram?" They said, "From al-'Aqiq."
He said, "You have attained the concession and followed the Sunnah."
And when two doors present themselves to me, both of which are permissible, I take the easier one.
And that is because God is easy-loving, loves what is easy, and gives for what is easy what He does not give for exertion/hardship.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ihram, the state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.مِنْ أَيْنَ أَحْرَمْتَ: From where did you enter Ihram (referring to the Miqat)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred Miqat for entering Ihram according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) critiques the practice of extending the Miqat distance for perceived greater reward or shrine visitation, labeling it as based on unreliable reports. He affirms that adhering to the closer, easier Miqat is the true Sunnah, illustrating the theological principle that God loves ease (*al-yasir*) and grants abundant reward for it, unlike the limited reward for strenuous effort (*al-'unf*). This highlights the Shia emphasis on following the Prophet's established practice over voluntary asceticism or innovation in ritual boundaries.
